title: Medicare ACCESS Model Eligibility Costs and Chronic Care Support
rawContent:
Key Takeaways
•	The ACCESS Model gives eligible people with Original Medicare another way to receive ongoing support for certain chronic conditions.
•	Services may include virtual visits, health coaching, medication management, behavioral health support, apps, and connected devices. The services available depend on the participating organization and your condition.
•	Most ACCESS organizations charge between $0 and $7 per month. A single organization cannot charge more than $13 per month when it supports you with multiple conditions.
•	You can contact a participating organization directly without a referral. You keep your existing doctors and other Original Medicare benefits.
•	Medicare Advantage members cannot participate in ACCESS, although their plans may offer similar programs.
The Medicare ACCESS Model helps people with Original Medicare manage certain chronic health conditions between regular medical appointments. It connects eligible patients with Medicare-approved organizations that may provide virtual care, coaching, remote monitoring, and other personalized support.
ACCESS does not replace your doctor or change your Medicare coverage. It adds condition-specific support to the care you already receive. Availability depends on your health condition, location, and the organizations participating in your area.
What Is the Medicare ACCESS Model
ACCESS stands for Advancing Chronic Care with Effective, Scalable Solutions. It is a 10-year Medicare Innovation Center model that began July 5, 2026.
The model gives participating healthcare organizations a new way to provide technology-supported care for chronic conditions. Instead of paying only for individual appointments or services, Medicare ties ACCESS payments to measurable health outcomes across the patients an organization serves.
For you, the practical difference is the opportunity to receive support between appointments. Depending on the organization, that may include help tracking blood pressure, managing medication, changing daily habits, or monitoring symptoms from home.
Participation is voluntary. Joining ACCESS does not reduce your Medicare benefits, limit your choice of Medicare providers, or require you to leave your primary care doctor or specialists. You can read the program details on the CMS ACCESS Model page.
Who Qualifies for the ACCESS Model
You may qualify when both of the following are true:
1.	You have Original Medicare.
2.	You have at least one health condition included in an ACCESS clinical track.
Having a listed condition does not mean that every participating organization can serve you. Each organization supports specific conditions and geographic areas. The organization will confirm your eligibility before your care begins.
You do not need a doctor’s referral to contact an ACCESS organization. Your doctor, pharmacist, or another healthcare provider may also help you find one. Medicare maintains a directory of participating ACCESS organizations with information about the conditions they support.
Which Conditions Are Included in ACCESS
ACCESS currently includes four broad clinical tracks. You may qualify with one or more of the following conditions:
Clinical track	Included conditions
Early cardio kidney metabolic conditions	High blood pressure, high cholesterol, obesity, overweight with a marker of central obesity, and prediabetes
Cardio kidney metabolic conditions	Diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease

Musculoskeletal conditions	Ongoing muscle or joint pain
Behavioral health conditions	Depression and anxiety
CMS may add conditions in the future. A participating organization may not offer every clinical track, so check the organization’s listing before signing up.
Conditions Being Added April 1 2027
CMS is expanding ACCESS on April 1, 2027, to include:
•	Heart failure
•	Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
•	Substance use disorders, including opioid and alcohol use disorders
•	Tobacco cessation
•	Extended support for certain chronic musculoskeletal conditions after the initial care period
These additions do not mean that every ACCESS organization will offer every new track on April 1. Check Medicare’s participant directory for the conditions and areas served by each organization. CMS announced the expansion on September 15, 2026, and explains the new tracks in its ACCESS expansion announcement.
What Services Can ACCESS Organizations Provide
The support you receive depends on your condition and the participating organization you choose. Available services may include:
•	Virtual visits with members of your care team
•	Nutrition, exercise, and lifestyle coaching
•	Apps that help you track symptoms or health goals
•	Connected devices or wearables
•	Medication management
•	Behavioral health support
•	Patient education and care coordination
•	Support for more than one chronic condition
Some organizations may lend you equipment related to your condition, such as a blood pressure monitor or continuous glucose monitor. Medicare says you will not have to pay to use this equipment, although you may need to return it later.
ACCESS can include virtual visits, but it is broader than standard Medicare telehealth coverage. An ACCESS organization may combine virtual care with monitoring, coaching, devices, medication support, and communication with your regular providers. The exact combination varies by organization.
How Much Does the Medicare ACCESS Model Cost
Most participating organizations charge between $0 and $7 per month. If one organization helps you manage multiple qualifying conditions, it cannot charge more than $13 per month total.
That $13 limit applies when a single organization supports you with multiple conditions. If you use separate organizations for different conditions, ask each one to explain its monthly charge before you enroll.
Your fee pays for the ACCESS support provided by that organization. It does not replace your regular Medicare costs, including your Part B premium, deductible, or cost-sharing for other covered healthcare services.
Some organizations may waive ACCESS cost-sharing. Because charges and services vary, ask for the following information before signing up:
•	The monthly amount you will owe
•	Which services and devices are included
•	Whether equipment must be returned
•	How the organization will coordinate with your doctors
•	Whether you will have any costs outside the monthly ACCESS charge
How to Find and Join an ACCESS Organization
You can enroll directly with a participating ACCESS organization. A referral is not required.
Follow these steps:
1.	Visit the Medicare ACCESS directory and search for participating organizations.
2.	Confirm that the organization supports your condition and serves your location.
3.	Review its services, technology requirements, monthly cost, and equipment policies.
4.	Ask how it will communicate with your primary care doctor and specialists.
5.	Contact the organization directly to enroll.
Your doctor, pharmacist, or another healthcare provider can help you compare participating organizations. If you manage several qualifying conditions, you may be able to use one organization for multiple conditions or work with more than one organization.
Before enrolling, consider whether you are comfortable using the organization’s app, devices, or virtual-care platform. Ask whether you will need a smartphone, internet connection, or help setting up equipment. These requirements can vary.
What Happens After You Sign Up
The ACCESS organization will confirm your eligibility and explain how its program works. It should also tell you what information it will collect, which services you will receive, and what you will pay.
The organization will create a care plan for your qualifying condition. When possible, it will share updates with your primary care doctor or specialists so your care remains coordinated. You will continue using your regular healthcare providers for appointments, treatments, and other Medicare-covered services.
Most ACCESS care is available on an ongoing basis. Participation remains voluntary, and you can cancel or switch organizations after your first 90 days. Ask the organization what happens to any loaned equipment and how your care information will be transferred if you leave.
ACCESS Compared With Chronic Care Management
ACCESS and Medicare Chronic Care Management can both help you manage ongoing health problems, but they are separate Medicare options.
Feature	ACCESS Model	Chronic Care Management
Who may qualify	People with Original Medicare and at least one condition included in an ACCESS track	People with two or more chronic conditions expected to last at least 12 months or until death and that create a significant health risk
Who provides the service	A Medicare-approved ACCESS organization	A physician or another qualified healthcare professional who manages your care
Type of support	Technology-supported condition management that may include coaching, monitoring, apps, devices, and virtual care	Care planning and coordination outside regular office visits
Enrollment	You can contact an ACCESS organization directly without a referral	Your healthcare provider obtains your consent and enrolls you in its Chronic Care Management service
Typical cost	Most organizations charge $0 to $7 per month, subject to the program’s limits	The Part B deductible and coinsurance may apply unless other coverage pays your share
Medicare Advantage	Not available through ACCESS	Medicare Advantage plans cover the underlying Part B service, although plan rules and costs can differ
You could meet the eligibility requirements for both options. Before using both, ask your healthcare provider and the ACCESS organization how they will coordinate your care and whether the services overlap.
Can Medicare Advantage Members Use ACCESS
No. ACCESS is currently limited to people with Original Medicare. You cannot enroll in the ACCESS Model if you have a Medicare Advantage plan.
Your Medicare Advantage plan may offer a similar chronic-condition program, virtual-care service, or remote monitoring benefit. Check your plan’s Evidence of Coverage or contact the plan directly to ask:
•	Whether it offers support for your condition
•	Which providers or vendors participate
•	Whether referrals or prior authorization are required
•	What copayments or other costs apply
•	Whether devices or monitoring equipment are included
Do not leave a Medicare Advantage plan solely to gain access to this program without reviewing the full consequences. Changing coverage can affect your provider network, prescription coverage, out-of-pocket costs, and ability to purchase a Medicare Supplement policy.
Is the ACCESS Model Right for You
ACCESS may be worth considering if you have Original Medicare, qualify through one of its clinical tracks, and want more support between medical appointments.
Before enrolling, compare organizations based on the details that affect your care:
•	Condition support: Confirm that the organization serves your specific condition.
•	Services: Ask what coaching, monitoring, appointments, apps, or devices you will actually receive.
•	Technology: Make sure you can use the required technology or receive setup assistance.
•	Care coordination: Find out how often the organization will communicate with your doctors.
•	Cost: Confirm the monthly charge and whether any other costs may apply.
•	Privacy: Ask how the organization will collect, use, and share your health information.
•	Cancellation: Review the 90-day commitment and equipment-return process.
The best fit depends on your health goals and the organizations available where you live. ACCESS is optional, so you can compare the available programs without changing your existing Medicare coverage or providers.
Frequently Asked Questions
Is ACCESS a New Medicare Plan
No. ACCESS is a Medicare Innovation Center model that provides additional support for certain chronic conditions. It does not replace Original Medicare, Medicare Supplement coverage, or Part D prescription drug coverage.
Do You Need a Referral for ACCESS
No. You can contact a participating organization and sign up directly. Your doctor, pharmacist, or another healthcare provider can also help you find an organization.
Can You Keep Your Doctors After Joining ACCESS
Yes. ACCESS does not replace your primary care doctor or specialists. You keep the right to visit any healthcare provider who accepts Medicare. The ACCESS organization may coordinate with your regular providers and share updates about your progress when possible.
Can You Use More Than One ACCESS Organization
You may be able to work with more than one organization if you have multiple qualifying conditions. Ask each organization about its services and monthly charges. The $13 monthly limit applies when one organization supports multiple conditions.
Can You Cancel ACCESS
Yes. Participation is voluntary. Medicare says you can cancel or switch organizations after your first 90 days. Ask how to return any loaned equipment before ending the service.
Does ACCESS Cover Heart Failure and COPD
ACCESS tracks for heart failure and COPD begin April 1, 2027. Availability will depend on which participating organizations offer those tracks in your area.
How to Take the Next Step
Start by checking Medicare’s ACCESS directory for an organization that supports your condition and serves your location. Compare its services, technology, costs, and approach to coordinating with your doctors before you enroll.
If you cannot find an appropriate organization or need help understanding the program, call 1-800-MEDICARE. If your larger question involves choosing between Original Medicare and Medicare Advantage, a licensed Medicare agent can help you compare coverage available in your area. Joining ACCESS itself does not require you to work with an insurance agent.

sections.text: A New Way to Get Support Between Doctor Visits

sections.content: Managing a chronic condition often means long stretches between appointments where you are on your own. A new blood pressure reading, a missed dose, or a worrying symptom can leave you wondering whether to call the doctor's office or just wait it out.

Starting July 5, 2026, Medicare launched a program designed to fill that gap. It is called the ACCESS Model, and it connects eligible people on Original Medicare with approved organizations that offer ongoing, technology-supported help for certain chronic conditions.

This program does not replace your doctor or change your existing Medicare benefits. It adds an extra layer of support, and whether it makes sense for you depends on your health condition, where you live, and which organizations serve your area.

sections.calloutText: ACCESS stands for Advancing Chronic Care with Effective, Scalable Solutions. It is a 10-year Medicare Innovation Center model that began July 5, 2026, and ties payments to health outcomes rather than individual visits.

sections.text: What Is the Medicare ACCESS Model

sections.content: ACCESS gives participating healthcare organizations a new way to provide technology-supported care for chronic conditions. Instead of billing Medicare only for individual services or appointments, these organizations are paid based on measurable health outcomes across the patients they serve.

For you, the practical benefit is support between appointments. Depending on the organization you choose, that might include help tracking blood pressure, managing medications, adjusting daily habits, or monitoring symptoms from home.

Joining ACCESS is entirely voluntary. It does not reduce your Medicare benefits, limit your choice of providers, or require you to leave your primary care doctor or specialists. You can review full program details on the CMS ACCESS Model page.

Having a qualifying condition does not guarantee that every organization can serve you, since each one supports specific conditions and geographic areas.
You do not need a doctor's referral to reach out to an ACCESS organization directly. Your doctor, pharmacist, or another provider can also help you find one that fits your needs.

sections.calloutText: Each participating organization confirms eligibility before care begins. Ask specifically whether it supports your condition and your zip code before assuming you qualify.
